q: 1. When the plastic limit cannot be determined, the soil is reported to be .............
explain: If the soil cannot be rolled into threads to determine plastic limit, it is classified as non-plastic.

q: 2. In the field, sand can be distinguished from silt by .............
explain: The dilatancy test shows a characteristic surface sheen reaction in sand and silty sand, helping distinguish sand from silt in the field.

q: 3. The soil which contains finest grain particles, is
explain: Clay has the smallest particle size (<0.002 mm) among the options, making it the finest-grained soil.

q: 4. The basis for all soil classification systems is
explain: Engineering soil classification (like USCS or AASHTO) primarily relies on grain size distribution and Atterberg limits (plasticity).

q: 5. The range of values printed on a hydrometer are .............
explain: Standard soil hydrometers used in sedimentation analysis are calibrated over roughly 0.995 to 1.040.

q: 6. The property of a soil which allows it to be deformed rapidly without rupture, elastic rebound and also a volume change, is known
explain: Plasticity is the property allowing rapid deformation without cracking, remoulding, and volume change, characteristic of fine-grained cohesive soils.

q: 7. The smallest sieve size according to Indian standards is .............
explain: The finest standard IS sieve size used in grain size analysis is 0.045 mm.

q: 8. A soil having particles of nearly the same size is known as .............
explain: A uniform soil has particles concentrated in a narrow size range, giving a low uniformity coefficient.

q: 9. In hydrometer analysis the principle used is
explain: Stokes' Law governs the terminal velocity of spherical particles falling through a liquid, which is the basis for hydrometer tests.

q: 10. The property of the soil which permits it to be deformed rapidly without volume change, rupture and elastic rebound is termed as .............
explain: Plasticity is the property that allows soil to be remoulded/deformed without volume change, cracking, or elastic rebound.

q: 11. When other factors remaining constant, the velocity with which as soil grain settle out of suspension depends upon .............
explain: As per Stoke's Law, settling velocity depends jointly on the grain's shape, size, and weight.

q: 12. Soil which contains the particles of different sizes in good proportion is called .............
explain: A well graded soil has a continuous, balanced distribution of particle sizes across a wide range.

q: 13. The ratio of plasticity index to flow index is called
explain: Toughness index (It) is defined as the ratio of the plasticity index to the flow index, indicating the shear strength of the soil at the plastic limit.

q: 14. Bearing capacity of soil depends up on the particle
explain: Bearing capacity is influenced by particle shape (interlocking), cohesion, and size (gradation/density) — collectively all these factors matter.

q: 15. Effective size of the particle is
explain: Effective size is defined as D10 — the particle size corresponding to 10% passing on the grain size distribution curve.

q: 16. The type of shear failure that can be expected for a loose sand (or) a soft clay is .............
explain: Loose sands and soft clays are highly compressible and tend to fail by punching shear, with large settlements and no distinct failure surface.

q: 17. The uniformity coefficient of soil is
explain: Uniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10, a measure of the range of particle sizes present (gradation).

q: 18. The standard penetration test is performed in a hole of diameter about .............
explain: SPT boreholes are typically drilled in the range of about 55 to 150 mm diameter to accommodate the split-spoon sampler and drilling equipment.

q: 19. The ratio of the unconfined compressive strength of undisturbed soil to the unconfined compressive strength of soil in a remoulded state, is called .............
explain: This ratio is the definition of sensitivity, indicating how much strength a clay loses upon remoulding.

q: 20. The sensitivity of a normal clay is about .............
explain: Normal (moderately sensitive) clays typically have sensitivity values in the range of about 2 to 4.

q: 21. The effective size of the soil is
explain: Effective size is standard defined as D10, the sieve size through which 10% of the soil (by weight) passes.

q: 22. Uniformity co-efficient is the ratio of
explain: Uniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10 by definition, indicating the range/spread of particle sizes.

q: 23. Plasticity index / Flow index is known as
explain: The ratio of plasticity index to flow index is termed the toughness index, indicating shear resistance of a soil at its plastic limit.

q: 24. Shrinkage index
explain: Shrinkage index is defined as the difference between liquid limit and shrinkage limit (Is = LL − SL), representing the moisture range for which the soil remains semi-solid to liquid.

q: 25. In an undrained plastic clay the shear strength is due to .............
explain: Under undrained conditions, saturated plastic clay exhibits an angle of friction close to zero, so its shear strength is governed by cohesion.

q: 26. A fine grained soil has
explain: Fine-grained soils (clays/silts) have small pore sizes restricting flow (low permeability) and a compressible, plastic structure (high compressibility).

q: 27. According to IS classification, the value of liquid limit for fine grained soils of high compressibility is .............
explain: IS classification uses LL = 50% as the boundary between low/intermediate and high compressibility fine-grained soils.

q: 28. In a hydrometer analysis the reason for addition of hydrogen peroxide and heating it is to remove .............
explain: Hydrogen peroxide oxidizes and removes organic matter, which would otherwise interfere with dispersion and settling of particles.

q: 29. In a hydrometer analysis for removing calcium compounds the following acid is used .............
explain: Dilute (0.2 N) hydrochloric acid is used to dissolve and remove calcium compounds before dispersion in hydrometer analysis.

q: 30. Which of the following clays behave like a dense sand .............
options: over consolidated clay with a low OCR
over consolidated clay with a high OCR
explain: Heavily over-consolidated clay (high OCR) exhibits dilative, brittle behaviour similar to dense sand under shear.

q: 31. The coarse grained soils will lie on boundary classification when they have this percentage of fines .............
explain: USCS boundary (dual) classification applies to coarse-grained soils with 5-12% fines content.

q: 32. Relative density of a compacted dense sand is approximately equal to
explain: A well-compacted, dense sand approaches its densest possible state (e close to emin), giving a relative density close to but just under 1.0, i.e., approximately 0.95.

q: 33. The deflocculating agent which is used in the sedimentation analysis is .............
explain: Sodium hexametaphosphate is the standard dispersing/deflocculating agent used to keep particles separated during sedimentation analysis.

q: 34. Uniformify co-efficient is the ratio of .............
explain: Uniformity coefficient Cu = D60/D10, comparing the 60% and 10% passing sizes.

q: 35. The slope of the flow curve obtained in liquid limit test is called .............
explain: The slope of the water content vs. log(number of blows) curve in the liquid limit test defines the flow index.

q: 36. If kerosene is used instead of water in the Pycnometer method of determination of grain specific gravity, the expression for the grain specific gravity .............
options: should be added to the sp. gravity of kerosene
should be multiplied by the sp. gravity of kerosene
should be divided by the sp. gravity of kerosene
should be subtracted by the sp. gravity of kerosene
explain: When kerosene replaces water (useful for gypsum/soluble soils), the result must be divided by kerosene's own specific gravity to reference it back to water.

q: 37. The maximum shear stress occurs on the filament which makes an angle with the horizontal plane equal to .............
explain: Maximum shear stress in a Mohr's circle analysis occurs on the plane inclined at 45° to the principal planes.

q: 38. The composite correction to be applied for in a hydrometer reading is .............
explain: The composite correction combines meniscus, dispersing agent, and temperature corrections in the specific signed combination C = Cm - Cd ± Ct.

q: 39. Samples from auger boring are .............
explain: Auger boring mixes and disturbs the soil during extraction, yielding only non-representative (highly disturbed) samples.

q: 40. With reference to shrinkage and swelling, the most active clay mineral is .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'none of these'; the standard, well-established fact is that montmorillonite is the most active (highest swelling/shrinkage) clay mineral.

q: 41. The difference between plastic limit and shrinkage limit is called .............
explain: Per the reference key, PL - SL is termed relative consistency in this classification (note: some texts call this the shrinkage index).

q: 42. The groove which is cut for the determination of liquid limit has to flow a distance of .............
explain: In the Casagrande liquid limit test, the two halves of the soil pat must flow together and close over a distance of 11 mm (1/2 inch).

q: 43. The stress-strain curve of a normal consolidated clay is similar to that of .............
explain: Normally consolidated clay shows a gradually rising, contractive stress-strain curve similar to loose sand.

q: 44. The activity of clay is defined as the ratio of .............
explain: Skempton's activity is defined as plasticity index divided by the percentage of clay-sized (<2 micron) fraction.

options: mixture of sand, silt and clay sized particles in equal proportions
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'silt with little sand'; loam is more commonly defined (as seen earlier for Q10) as a balanced mixture of sand, silt, and clay.

q: 46. The symbol OH indicates .............
options: organic silts and organic silts of high plasticity
explain: In USCS notation, OH denotes organic clay/silt of high plasticity.

q: 47. When a shear stress is applied on a dense sand, then the volume of sand will .............
explain: Dense sand dilates (increases in volume) under shear as densely packed grains ride over one another.
